base_member_text: [L17-L32] (LOW/error-handling) The distribution script performs destructive recursive removal and multiple wildcard copies without checking command success, so a missing input, failed mkdir, or copy error can still yield an apparently completed but incomplete distribution.
audit_member_text: [L18-L32] (MED/error-propagation) The previous distribution is removed before validating inputs and copy failures are unchecked, so a final successful license copy can conceal an incomplete package.
[L18-L19] (MED/build-order-coupling) The executable post-build deletes the entire shared distribution directory, including library DLLs published by the library post-build scripts.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: Lines 18-19 recursively remove and recreate the entire configuration distribution directory, without preserving library artifacts. The subsequent copies use only the executable TargetDir and static-library DLL directory, whereas the library publisher places XBeach.Library.dll and XBeach.BMI.dll in this same distribution directory.

adversarial.rationale: Both executable projects call this script as their post-build event, and the solution makes the executable, dynamic DLL and BMI DLL siblings depending on the static library (XBeach_VS2010.sln:3-30). The recursive distribution-directory removal therefore can erase DLLs already published by a sibling, while the following copy reads only the static-library/runtime DLL directory and executable TargetDir, not the published dynamic/BMI DLLs.

audit_member_text: [L22,L25-L26] (MED/stale-packaging) TargetDir is never cleared before wildcard packaging, allowing stale executables and DLLs from earlier builds to enter the new distribution.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: The script clears dist but never clears TargetDir; line 22 only adds or overwrites DLLs there. Lines 25-26 then copy every executable and DLL in TargetDir, including files left by earlier builds.
